applies_why: The judge uses the fact that a word/verse does not by itself establish begetting as a reason to leave the point open and mark it UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: D4 vs C3 (Luke 2:48): UNDERDETERMINED -- C3’s “thy father” is a plain register, but [CR3] answers that the narrator avoids “father” and the word does not by itself establish begetting; read together the fact of begetting remains open -- GROUND: C3 narrows away the claim that the word names a begetter, so it does not contradict D4’s supposition point.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: does not state a link or its contrary — I weighed whether it covers only an explicit statement or also a verse/word that does not by itself establish the link; I read it to cover the latter.
why: D4 is marked UNDERDETERMINED because the word does not by itself establish begetting, which is the forbidden use of a single verse's non-statement as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.
